extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscientists, psychologists, and researchers studying humor and sex/gender differences using fMRI
extracted.subtask_short: fMRI study of humor sex/gender differences
extracted.subtask_description: Event-related fMRI experiment and analysis protocol for comparing neural correlates of three verbal joke types (bridging-inference, exaggeration, ambiguity) between women and men, including stimulus selection, behavioral validation, acquisition, preprocessing, ROI/statistical analysis, and confirmatory checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant inclusion and demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Twenty-six healthy volunteers (13 women; mean age 24.27 ± 2.18; range 22–29). All participants were native Mandarin speakers, right-handed, and had no history of neurological or psychiatric problems. Handedness determined by the Edinburgh handedness inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control for age and education between sexes/genders; obtain written informed consent in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki; sample sizes and demographic matching reported and tested (t-tests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus composition and counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Stimuli: 80 jokes in Mandarin Chinese including 30 bridging-inference jokes (BJs), 20 exaggeration jokes (EJs), and 30 ambiguity jokes (AJs). Corresponding baseline conditions: 30 bridging-inference baselines (BS), 20 exaggeration baselines (ES), 30 ambiguity baselines (AS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baselines constructed by replacing punch lines with neutral (unfunny) stories of matching length and punctuation; few EJs used because dataset excluded nonsense jokes and jokes related to psychiatric hospitals and patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke-type definitions (logical mechanisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bridging-inference jokes (BJs): use the 'inferring consequences' logical mechanism where key point is not explicitly stated and requires backward inferencing/theory of mind. Exaggeration jokes (EJs): use the 'exaggeration' mechanism creating semantic distortion (features much bigger/smaller than expected). Ambiguity jokes (AJs): use the 'juxtaposition' mechanism to generate linguistic ambiguity (double meanings requiring disambiguation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different joke types call upon different cognitive processes for comprehension and appreciation; EJs involve semantic distortion, AJs linguistic ambiguity, BJs require inferencing to comprehend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus selection and validation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes selected from a database of Chinese jokes or websites. Behavioral pilot studies were conducted to ensure validity: participants rated each trial on a 9-point comprehensibility scale (mean 8.25 ± 0.83) and funniness (mean 6.06 ± 1.65).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose stimuli with high comprehensibility; use pilot ratings and one-way repeated-measures ANOVA with post hoc tests to confirm funny vs unfunny conditions differ significantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-scanner behavioral measure (funniness rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: During scanning participants provided a subjective funniness judgment by pressing one of four buttons (1 = 'not funny at all' to 4 = 'very funny').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand used for button-press responses counterbalanced in the scanner; report mean funniness ratings and run repeated-measures ANOVA to test effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental paradigm timing and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Event-related paradigm: jittered ISI randomly varied among 2.1, 3.2, 5.6, 7.9 s; setup shown for 12 s; punch line delivered for 9 s; five functional runs; first three TRs discarded per run; each run lasted 8 min 4 s; total duration ~48 min 6 s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present stimuli using E-Prime in black and white; model the punch line as the event of interest; counterbalance and randomize trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline construction principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding baseline conditions were constructed by replacing the punch lines with neutral (unfunny) stories of matching length and punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use baselines that match non-humorous linguistic features (length, punctuation) to isolate humor-related processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image acquisition parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional images on a 3-tesla MRI (Siemens Skyra) with 32-channel head coil. Every volume contained 32 transversal slices (4-mm-thick, no gap) TR = 2000 ms, TE = 30 ms, flip angle = 90°, FOV 240 × 240 mm, matrix 64 × 64 (in-plane spatial resolution = 3.75 mm). Structural T1 MPRAGE: TR = 1900 ms, TE = 3.30 ms, flip angle = 9°, 256 × 256 matrix, 192 slices, 1 mm isotropic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report scanner model, coil, slice orientation (parallel to AC-PC), and full acquisition parameters to permit replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing pipeline and motion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: fMRI preprocessing: timing reslicing, realignment, co-registration to anatomical image, normalization to standard MNI T1 template, spatial smoothing with an 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel, high-pass filter (128-s cutoff), slice-acquisition time correction to middle volume. Movement no more than 3 mm in any plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include motion thresholds and exclude/flag runs or participants exceeding movement limits; report smoothing kernel and high-pass cutoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-level GLM modeling choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Event-related GLM: functions corresponding to onset of different event types were convolved with a canonical hemodynamic response function (HRF) and its temporal derivative. Stimuli treated as individual events and modeled for the punch line. Six motion parameters included as regressors of no interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model the punch line as the key event; include temporal derivative to account for HRF variability; include motion regressors to reduce motion-related artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-of-interest (ROI) strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Anatomical ROI maps generated using WFU PickAtlas; analyses focused on 8 predefined ROIs: aPFC (BA 10), dPFC (BA 9/8), TPJ (BA 39), amygdala, parahippocampal gyrus (PHG), insula (BA 13), orbitofrontal cortex (OFC; BA 11/47), and supplementary motor area (SMA; BA 6). Midbrain region included given role in affective modulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a priori ROIs based on prior research, report BA labels and coordinates, and indicate ROI creation tool and masks used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level statistical design
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameter estimates entered into a second-level random effects analysis using a flexible factorial design to test between-group inferences. Between-group analysis conducted using a two-way mixed ANOVA parsing main effect of joke type (BJ-BS vs EJ-ES vs AJ-AS), main effect of sex/gender (women vs men), and interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use flexible factorial to model within- and between-subject factors appropriately and report exact design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical thresholding and multiple comparison correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Threshold of activation for predefined ROIs set at a voxel-wise p < 0.05 FWE (family-wise error rate) corrected for multiple comparisons with five contiguous voxels using a small volume correction (SVC) and using a 10-mm sphere on the coordinates of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify correction method (FWE with SVC), voxel extent threshold (five contiguous voxels), and sphere radius for SVC (10 mm); report exact p-values and Z-scores for peaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect size and time-series reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Time-series analysis conducted to determine between-group differences in magnitude of percent signal change (PSC). The study used PSC to describe sex/gender effect magnitude and mean beta values in between-group analyses; event-related responses plotted in peri-stimulus time bins with fitted response and PSTH (mean ± SE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report PSC, beta/contrast estimates, and consider Cohen's d; extract peak voxels and plot peri-stimulus time courses to visualize hemodynamic differences between groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmatory/randomization and within-group variance checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses performed on randomly assigned participants in two random groups and within-group variance analyses for women and men to provide additional checks on whether sex/gender differences could be due to chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include random group analysis and within-group variance metrics as robustness checks when reporting group differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: A priori hypotheses about region × joke-type × sex/gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypotheses: women would show greater TPJ activation than men for BJs (ToM), women would display increased aPFC activation than men for EJs and AJs (executive control/language decoding), men would show stronger dPFC activation (goal-directed monitoring), women greater OFC activation for BJs and greater amygdala/midbrain activation for EJs, men greater PHG for AJs, and women increased SMA (BA 6) suggesting expressive laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear region-specific hypotheses before analysis to justify ROI approach and interpret interaction effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROI reporting conventions and coordinate reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report BA, voxel counts, MNI coordinates (x, y, z), Z-scores, and side for main effects and interactions (as shown in tables). Activation threshold for simple main effects set at p < 0.05 FWE within eight predefined ROIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tables with BA, voxel extent, MNI coordinates, Z-scores and indicate frequencies/percentages of activation in women vs men when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of behavioral measures to interpret neural results
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral funniness ratings (in-scanner 4-point scale) and pilot comprehensibility/funniness measures used to interpret neural activations; report main effects and interactions for behavioral data (ANOVAs, effect sizes ηp2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always report behavioral validation and test whether neural differences align with behavioral differences (e.g., main effect of joke type, sex/gender effects, interaction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion/artifact control in first-level GLM
rubrics_metrics.description: To increase statistical sensitivity and remove motion-related artifacts, include six motion parameters as regressors of no interest in the first-level GLM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report inclusion of motion regressors and state movement thresholds (<=3 mm) and any additional denoising steps used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus presentation software and display details
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental paradigm presented using E-Prime; all stimuli presented in black and white on a projector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify presentation software and display settings to facilitate replication and timing reproducibility.
